column3: Identifies the same disbelief in God and messenger as a lasting disqualifying state.
Adds a distant transfer-and-coercion frame, not the acceptance of willing worship.
Connects non-acceptance with a broken religious orientation.
Directly joins lazy prayer with outward display and concealed insincerity.
Opens the nearby sequence where excuses expose truthfulness and falsehood.
Shows resistance to the truth, but not its effect on worship or acceptance.
Contrasts their spending with expenditure recorded for those who act faithfully.
Directly states that spending, willing or unwilling, is not accepted from them.
Only broadly parallels aversion to truth.
Shows minimal participation by obstructers, without the acceptance question.
Explains the surrounding resentment over alms and self-interested satisfaction.
Shows a claimed superiority functioning as an inner barrier to commanded action.
Places their unwillingness within prior efforts to upset the truth.
Adds an indirect giving-hand channel without clarifying their rejected deeds.
Reiterates disbelief but adds little after the clearer early evidence.
Adds false oaths, disbelief after profession, and resentment despite received bounty.
Contrasts believers' readiness to strive with wealth and selves against their excuses.
Shows disbelief joined to wrongdoing as a continuing relational closure.
Gives the positive pairing of established prayer and spending from provision.
Supplies the contrary disposition of contentment, trust, and desire toward God.
Broadens obstruction from personal withholding to blocking access to good.
Links deepened disbelief to a stated non-acceptance, though of repentance.
Qualifies their wealth and children as part of their worldly affliction while disbelieving.
Pairs maintaining prayer with asking for acceptance, in a different act.
Reinforces the positive prayer-and-spending pattern already established.
Adds withdrawal and dismissal of the message, only indirectly related.
Restates persistent disbelief without adding to the mechanism of 9:54.
Shows hostility to believers for faith, without worship or acceptance.
Makes their request for exemption arise from unbelief and unsettled hearts.
Clarifies the question form: a stated barrier can be sought for omitted intervention.
Uses the same barrier formulation for faith and seeking forgiveness.
Shows a self-serving excuse that is itself the fall into trial.
The contrast link marks a boundary; the verse adds no usable support here.
Contrasts scant obedience with the stabilizing effect of doing what is urged.
Opposes withholding and calls for continued giving and pardon.
Its contrast route is boundary evidence and its topic does not clarify 9:54.
Pairs preventing others with withdrawing oneself from the message.
Directly connects lack of resolve to failure to prepare and being held back from departure.
Only restates rejection after a reminder arrives.
Shows organized prayer under danger, but not the inward condition of 9:54.
Adds their frantic turning toward escape rather than commitment.
A distant acceptance image with no clear bearing on their rejected expenditure.
Directly shows disbelievers' wealth cannot become an accepted payment.
Only indirectly touches distorted desire through a channel resonance.
Adds a general image of unobstructed provision, not their worship.
Distinguishes genuine incapacity from blameworthy refusal when loyalty is sincere.
Shows why their participation would be corrupting rather than beneficial.
Parallels obstruction of worship, but not the inward cause of non-acceptance.
Offers a further positive profile joining faith, prayer, and almsgiving.
The channel's desire theme is too remote from the focus.
Shows a prayer-form reduced to empty performance amid disbelief.
Warns that apparent good work can be fundamentally misdirected.
Adds their pleasure at harm and turning away within the same surrounding portrait.
Directly contrasts God's receiving alms with acceptance of repentance.
Uses the same barrier form and shows denial shaping what is sent.
Tests whether claimed affiliation is matched by action and undivided allegiance.
Directly states that disliking what God sent renders deeds void.
Specifies recipients of good expenditure, not acceptance or disposition.
The gate image has no material connection to the focus.
Shows visible bodily approach can coexist with inward rejection.
Does not illuminate acceptance, prayer, spending, or their inner resistance.
Sets the trustful stance of believers within the immediate sequence.
Only generally identifies what is disliked by God.
Links aversion to truth with a dismissive accusation against its bearer.
Frames preferring disbelief over faith as a disqualifying allegiance choice.
Connects disbelief and obstructing God's way with ruined works.
Offers a distant example of misplaced security against God.
Gives a composite positive disposition including devoted spending.
Qualifies aversion: reluctance alone does not determine an act's true good.
Reiterates widespread aversion to truth already supplied more directly.
Continues the immediate contrast between believers' expectation and their hostile waiting.
Adds general lying and rejection of truth, with little new for 9:54.
Shows that completed sacred work still seeks God's acceptance.
Adds an adjacent false belief but not the focus's acts or their reception.
Restates hardened disbelief without clarifying rejected worship.
Addresses unsupported false worship, only broadly related to disbelief.
Touches provision and worldly delight, but not spending's acceptance.
Adds surprise at warning as a remote form of disbelief.
Directly identifies withholding ordinary aid as a blockage of social good.
Adds their false claimed membership and fear in the same local portrait.
Directly establishes that an offering's acceptance depends on the offerer's piety.
Only states the outcome for disbelievers.
The branch resonance concerns diversion but adds no focused evidence.
Shows a prior assumption about the messenger blocking response to guidance.
Gives the positive integrated pattern of striving, prayer, almsgiving, and reliance.
A distant false-direction resonance without a focused contribution.
Shows aversion and self-serving false speech distorting the relation to God.
Does not address the focus's acceptance or inward condition.
Presents patience for God's sake with prayer and private or public spending.
Restates unsupported false worship and disbelief without new leverage.
Directly contrasts spoken profession with unbelieving hearts and manipulative response.
Reinforces that rejecting faith in God and messenger is a relational rupture.
Shows expenditure in God's way fully accounted for, contrasting their rejected spending.
Only generally concerns one who was denied.
Does not clarify their worship, expenditure, or acceptance.
Adds a remote social persistence of disbelief.
Only notes that many recipients of prophetic inheritance are wicked.
Denies an exemption for disbelievers but adds no focused mechanism.
Shows prayer and giving alongside recognized hardship and eased obligation.
Adds rejection of meeting God, but only indirectly bears on 9:54.
Directly links ostentatious spending without faith to the loss of its value.
Provides the positive faith-prayer-giving pattern with assured recompense.
Adds willing spending in ease and hardship within a disciplined moral disposition.
Makes costly giving a threshold for a higher good.
Directly joins showy expenditure with lack of faith in God and the Last Day.
Shows hostile expenditure becoming regret and defeat rather than beneficial action.
Identifies hypocritical withholding alongside forgetting God and moral reversal.
Opens their pledge to spend gratefully if granted abundance.
Shows bounty answered by stinginess and turning away.
Connects their broken spending pledge and falsehood to enduring hypocrisy.
Adds contempt for both voluntary donors and those with only limited means.
Shows spending regarded as a burden by some whose relation is hostile.
Contrasts this with spending sought as nearness to God and the messenger's prayer.
Directly connects taking alms with purification and the messenger's prayer.
Shows a worship site founded on harm, disbelief, and division despite its outward form.
Contrasts it with a worship site founded on piety and people seeking purification.
Links neglect of prayer with following desires in a later generation.
Sets steadfast maintenance of prayer against intermittent or reluctant performance.
Introduces the successful believers as the positive frame for the following acts.
Specifies humility within prayer, contrasting empty outward performance.
Includes active giving as a mark of the successful believers.
Shows trade and sale not diverting people from remembrance, prayer, and almsgiving.
Gives measured expenditure as an alternative to distorted financial conduct.
Pairs prayer and hidden or open spending with a non-perishing return.
Shows refusal to spend from God's provision coupled with dismissive unbelief.
Adds consultation, maintained prayer, and shared expenditure as a positive pattern.
Frames spending as a trust-based response to provision held in succession.
Distinguishes the moral weight of spending across costly circumstances.
Joins charitable giving with repentance, prayer, and almsgiving after reluctance.
Directly warns that wealth and children can distract from remembrance of God.
Urgently calls for spending before delay makes it impossible.
Links reverent obedience with spending for one's own good.
Frames giving as a good loan answered by multiplied return and forgiveness.
Begins the contrary disposition of anxious grasping and withholding.
Sets persistent prayer as the exception to that grasping disposition.
Identifies a recognized due in wealth, supplying the positive spending counterpart.
Names the recipients of that recognized due, completing the contrast to withholding.
Introduces the retrospective account of the causes of punishment.
Names failure to be among those who pray.
Joins that failure to prayer with failure to feed the needy.
Shows feeding others despite attachment to the food, a contrary willingness frame.
Combines purified devotion with prayer and almsgiving as the right religious orientation.
Directly warns against a category of people who pray.
Qualifies that warning through heedlessness regarding their prayer.
Adds performative display as the inward distortion of their worship.
